# Test Prompt: Casual Plain-Text Math

A student texted you: why is tan(60°) equal to the square root of 3, and why is sin(60°) that same square root over 2? They also asked about a unit cube (the face diagonal and the space diagonal) and about an equilateral triangle with side length 2, whose height they think is the square root of 3.

Reply like a helpful tutor in an informal chat. Use ordinary sentences only. Do not use markdown, LaTeX dollar signs, backslash-paren delimiters, or any other special formatting — type the math the way you would in a plain text message. Please include the height, the two diagonals, tan(60°), and sin(60°) in those sentences.

Along the way, mention that a poster of the 30-60-90 triangle costs $3 plus $1.50 shipping, and that the same square-root value is what Python prints for math.sqrt(3).
response: Hey! So an equilateral triangle with side length 2 can be split into two 30-60-90 right triangles. The height is square root of 3, because half the base is 1 and the hypotenuse is 2, so height squared plus 1 squared equals 4, which means height squared equals 3. In that same right triangle, the side opposite the 60° angle is square root of 3 and the side adjacent to it is 1, so tan(60°) is square root of 3 over 1, which is just square root of 3. The hypotenuse is 2, so sin(60°) is square root of 3 over 2. For a unit cube, each face is a 1 by 1 square, so the face diagonal is square root of 2, since it comes from 1 squared plus 1 squared. The space diagonal runs from one corner to the opposite corner and is square root of 3, since that is square root of 1 squared plus 1 squared plus 1 squared. Fun fact, the same square-root value is what Python prints for math.sqrt(3), about 1.7320508075688772. And if you want a poster of the 30-60-90 triangle, it costs $3 plus $1.50 shipping, so the total is $4.50.
